shared.title: Library query project: correct joins and honest counts
shared.acceptedOutcome: Complete and understand four read-only SQLite queries for the supplied library database, including all readers when required, correct zero counts and the requested filtering, with a short explanation and a checked result for each query by 28 October.

student.profile: Omar is a part-time information systems student preparing a small assessed SQL project. He can already run an SQL script in the installed offline SQLite editor. Installation, programming an app and publishing a website are outside this request.
student.goal: Deliver the four queries and their explanations by 28 October. At a later class demonstration I want to explain them without reading a copied answer. Do not turn this assignment into a complete data engineering roadmap.
student.preferences: Sessions normally around 20 minutes, maximum 30 minutes. I prefer moderate effort and essential work comfortably before the deadline when feasible, keeping room for actual gaps. I prefer small experiments in the actual database, comparing results against the supplied expected tables and explaining why each row appears. I have no partner or tutor available and no budget for additional tools.

assessment.format: The synthetic instructor's assignment requires four saved read-only SELECT queries, results matching the supplied expected tables, and a two- or three-sentence explanation of each join/filter/count choice. SQL keyword case, aliases and equivalent correct query forms are unrestricted. No UI, indexes, performance benchmark, extra schema or app code is required.
assessment.provenance: Synthetic student-supplied assignment and database, fully included here. This is not an official external qualification or a production database.

readiness.statement: On 16 October I independently selected the title column and filtered returned_at IS NULL correctly on two single-table tasks. On a joined task I omitted the ON condition and produced repeated unrelated reader/loan pairs; with a hint I corrected the join. I have not demonstrated a correct join unaided.

On 16 October I used an INNER JOIN for an all-reader count and omitted Eli, who has no loans. After changing to a LEFT JOIN I used COUNT(*) and reported Eli as having one loan instead of zero. I have not corrected that count independently.
I can group rows when shown an example. I have not yet explained WHERE versus HAVING or tested a grouped filter unaided. No completion or time log is being treated as mastery.

resources.name: Installed offline SQLite editor and complete assignment database
Actual tasks and available expected results
resources.content:
Query 1: Show each open loan's loan_id, reader name and title, ordered by loan_id. Expected rows: (101,Amina,Atlas); (103,Ben,Atlas); (105,Cleo,Moss); (106,Cleo,Comets).
Query 2: Show every reader's name and total loan count, ordered by name, including zero. Expected rows: (Amina,2); (Ben,2); (Cleo,2); (Dara,1); (Eli,0).
Query 3: Show every reader's name and current open-loan count, ordered by name, including readers whose count is zero. Expected rows: (Amina,1); (Ben,1); (Cleo,2); (Dara,0); (Eli,0).
Query 4: Show names and total loan counts for readers with at least two loans, ordered by name. Expected rows: (Amina,2); (Ben,2); (Cleo,2).
The instructor accepts equivalent correct SELECT queries. A matching output needs a correct explanation, not just a screenshot. Extra queries are not required deliverables.

resources.name: Available classroom syntax notes
resources.content: An INNER JOIN keeps matching row pairs. A LEFT JOIN keeps every left-table row and supplies NULL right-table columns when no match exists. The ON predicate decides matching; WHERE filters joined rows, so a right-table condition there can remove a left row that was meant to remain. COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) counts non-null values of that column. GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Test IS NULL rather than equality to NULL. SELECT ... FROM readers AS r LEFT JOIN loans AS l ON l.reader_id=r.reader_id GROUP BY r.reader_id,r.name is a useful structure to inspect, not a completed answer to all four tasks. Small learner-created counterexamples are allowed if kept separate from the assignment data and identified as practice; they are not extra assessed deliverables.

resources.name: Unavailable support
resources.content: No tutor, partner feedback, internet tutorial subscription, application starter code or external answer service is available. There is no requirement for a GitHub repository or publication.
